transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Mariner - Head of Search), Tom Ridley (Mariner CTO), Elena Gutierrez (Mariner ML Eng)

Auto Summary: quick discovery on embeddings and reranking; discuss vector DB options (Pinecone/Weaviate/Qdrant), embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, throughput targets (~200 qps), and security (VPC, SOC2, KMS). Redwood proposes a 2-day bench and follow-up technical deep dive.

00:00 Sofia Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh yeah i'm sofia from redwood inference, i'm the AE on the account, with diego from our se team. quick round robin?
01:00 Priya Nair: hey i'm priya thanks, head of search at mariner. we run search for our docs and clinical knowledge base, latency matters.
02:00 Tom Ridley: tom here, cto. we'll be the decision owner for infra questions.
03:00 Diego Ramos: cool, thanks. quick context question — what are you using today for embeddings and vector store?
04:00 Elena Gutierrez: currently prototyping with openai embeddings piped into pinecone, but we're hitting cost and variability issues; index size ~3M vectors, mostly 1536 dim, mixed short+long queries.
05:00 Priya Nair: and we do hybrid search: bm25 for recall then embeddings rerank top-100. looking to push to rerank top-1k ideally.
06:00 Sofia Chen: got it, that helps. our Hosted API supports embeddings and reranking, Dedicated gives reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need data residency. any particular security blockers?
07:00 Tom Ridley: SOC2 is table stakes, we also need KMS integration and audit logs. can you do SAML/SSO?
08:00 Diego Ramos: yes to SOC2 and SAML. KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted can integrate w/ customer-managed keys in certain enterprise plans. audit logs and per-route tracing are standard in our console.
09:00 Priya Nair: performance wise we care about tail latency under 150ms for rerank per query, with 200 qps sustained during business hours. how would that look on Hosted vs Dedicated?
10:00 Sofia Chen: rough rule — Hosted is great for lower or spiky traffic and fastest time-to-value; for sustained 200 qps reranking you'd probably look at Dedicated to reserve GPU pools. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and autoscaling policies.
11:00 Diego Ramos: for reranking, a lot depends on embedding dim and candidate count. reranking 1k candidates with a 1536-d embedding and cosine sim will be heavier than re-ranking 100 with 768. we can quantize and use CPU-friendly kernels for nearest neighbors on the index side too.
12:00 Elena Gutierrez: curious about vector DB options — we use Pinecone now, but we'd consider Milvus or Weaviate. does Redwood integrate with these or do you host your own index?
13:00 Sofia Chen: Redwood exposes embeddings and vector ops; many customers push embeddings into Pinecone/Weaviate/Qdrant/Milvus. Redwood can also host nearest-neighbor serving as part of Private deployments. Integration is mostly via SDK/webhooks or S3 export; we have examples for Pinecone and Milvus.
14:00 Priya Nair: any guidance on dimensionality — we currently have 1536 (OpenAI default). is there a sweet spot for tradeoff of cost vs quality?
15:00 Diego Ramos: yes — higher dims often give marginal quality gains past a point but increase index size and search cost roughly linearly. some teams reduce to 768 or 1024 with little loss depending on domain. we recommend running a small eval set to measure embedding AUC/ndcg vs dim. our Optimize tooling can recommend quantization and dimension reductions.
16:00 Tom Ridley: what about hybrid search? we want BM25 to surface recall then vector rerank; can Redwood help implement that pipeline?
17:00 Sofia Chen: absolutely — we typically recommend a two-stage approach: fast BM25 to fetch top-N then rerank references using embeddings served either via Hosted or Dedicated. Redwood's SDK includes helper patterns for fetch+rerank and we can show latency breakdowns per route in the console.
18:00 Elena Gutierrez: throughput numbers — what kind of QPS can Dedicated support for reranking 1k candidates?
19:00 Diego Ramos: depends on model footprint and whether metrics are pre-embedded/cached. if you pre-compute document embeddings and use an optimized ANN index you can get fairly high throughput; for 1k candidates and similarity only, a GPU-backed Dedicated pool can handle hundreds of QPS, but cost-wise many customers prefer reranking top-100 on GPU and do candidate expansion on CPU scalable index for larger candidate sets.
20:00 Priya Nair: we also need per-tenant data isolation and retention controls — Private or Dedicated?
21:00 Sofia Chen: Dedicated gives compute isolation (reserved pools) and data separation; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you network-level isolation and customer-managed control plane for compliance-heavy customers. retention and deletion policies are configurable across tiers.
22:00 Tom Ridley: we may need an on-prem option down the line for certain clinical customers. how does that impact rollout?
23:00 Diego Ramos: on-prem involves our private package, deployment automation, and we work with your infra team on KMS and logging. it's a longer lead time — usually multi-week to onboard.
24:00 Priya Nair: bench idea — can you run an ingest + rerank benchmark against 10k sample docs, mimic our 200 qps traffic for p95 latency?
25:00 Sofia Chen: yes, we can. typical plan: customer provides sample docs and query mix, we run a 48-hour benchmark on Dedicated capacity to measure end-to-end latency and cost. share results and recommended config (batching, quantization, index type).
26:00 Elena Gutierrez: sounds good. what about cost estimates? we need both per-token embedding cost and per-query ANN cost for vector search.
27:00 Diego Ramos: we'll provide a cost model in the pricing sheet — we include embedding units, ANN storage/ops (if using managed vector DB) and Dedicated capacity monthly commit options. for Hosted we can project per-1000-query cost.
28:00 Priya Nair: any gotchas with model versions and rollouts? we need ability to pin a model and do canary for rerank changes.
29:00 Sofia Chen: supported — you can pin model versions, do canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback to cheaper variants. all accessible in the Redwood Console.
30:00 Tom Ridley: regarding security, we need SOC2 report and SOC2 cop with encryption in transit and at rest. can you send security docs?
31:00 Sofia Chen: i'll send SOC2, ISO certs and our security whitepaper. we'll include details on KMS, SSO, and audit logs.
32:00 Elena Gutierrez: for NN search, metricwise we use cosine but we might experiment with dotprod for dense retrieval. any impact?
33:00 Diego Ramos: cosine and dotprod are functionally similar given normalized embeddings; implementation detail may affect latency on some kernels. we'll test both as part of the benchmark if you want.
34:00 Priya Nair: ok next steps?
35:00 Sofia Chen: recap — i'll send pricing + SKUs, security docs, and an initial bench plan. diego will send the benchmark scripts and requirements. elena to share 10k doc subset and query patterns. we aim to run bench next week.
36:00 Tom Ridley: timeline works, we'll try to get the dataset to you by monday.
37:00 Sofia Chen: great, we'll schedule the technical deep dive once bench plan is shared. thanks everyone.
38:00 Priya Nair: thanks all, that was helpful.
39:00 [call ends]
